question: What is a ‘Gopura’ in South Indian temple architecture of the medieval period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**An entrance gateway.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• It is also known as **Gopuram.**
 
• It is a** **large pyramidal tower over the entrance gate to a temple area.
 
• In the north India side it is called **Shikhara.**__
 
• The temple cities found it expedient **to build a series of protective walls to safeguard and defend their temples, cities and places.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nagara:__ **which temples located in **Northern India **are listed as **Nagara Style.**

 __
 
• **​**The architecture of Nagara Style has** multiple shikharas.**
 
• **Multiple Towers **in Nagara Style.
 
• The Central Tower is **Curvilinear** in Shape.
 
• In Nagara Style doesn't give much importance to the temple boundaries, and the deities are kept** inside.**
 
 
 
• Dravida:__ which temples located in **South**ern India are listed as **Dravid**a Style.
 __
 
• ​The architecture of Dravida Style has single shikhara.
 
• Single Towers in Dravida Style.
 
• The Central Tower is **Pyramid** in Shape.
 
• In Dravida Style are given high importance to the temple boundaries, and the deities are kept **outside.****​**
 
 

 
• **Vesara:__** emphasis is on **Viman and Mandapa.**

 
 
• **The Kailashnath Temple, Ellora, Chennakesava temple, Virupaksha Temple, and Ladkhan Temple** are famous temples of Vesara Style.
